unresolved: Crown reads as a sparse starburst of about 20-25 thin, short, mostly straight fronds. It is not a dense, rounded hemisphere of long arching fronds with a drooping lower tier (both seeds).
Fronds are far too thin and short, as the owner flagged. The leaflets are tiny relative to the rachis, so each frond reads as a bristly wire, not a broad plumose feather.

Trunk is strongly wavy. Seed 1 has a pronounced multi-bend S-curve that doubles back under the crown; seed 42 has a sharp mid-trunk kink and zigzag. This breaks the owner's straight or gently leaning requirement.
Trunk surface is smooth, with sparse, evenly spaced cylindrical peg stubs. There is no dense spiral diamond or rhomboid lattice of blunt, wedge-shaped leaf bases.
No fibrous matting between the leaf bases; the trunk is a clean, smooth cylinder.
No skirt of dead brown fronds under the living crown in either seed.
The P-BASE render is almost empty: sky and ground only, with the trunk clipped in the lower-right corner. The close-range leaf-base view can't be assessed.
